weekly:
Tiga R&D report, 2026-W46

Sent this week: 0; replies 0 (0 interested); drafts waiting for you: 47

Research notes: This week I ran two searches, on 2026 local SEO and GBP ranking factors, and on how freelancers package services for local businesses in India. I opened the Whitespark 'what's working in local SEO' survey, but only the first part of a very long page. I also opened one Mumbai freelancer's pricing page. The freelancer-marketplace results were mostly self-promotion, so I treated them as competitor examples only. I did not search on cold email or WhatsApp deliverability, Tiga tooling or comparable assistants. Cold-email timing and batch size are already on the board, and the 47 drafts waiting for approval remain the main blocker.

PROPOSALS
- [numbers] No mail went out this week: Find leads, draft and approve emails; check the daily cap and the approval backlog.
- [numbers] Approval backlog: 47 drafts waiting: Approve or reject drafts, or reduce how many leads are drafted per day.
- [numbers] Stabilise: No mail went out this week (seen 4 times): Repeating failure. Investigate the root cause rather than the symptom.
- [numbers] Stabilise: Approval backlog: 15 drafts waiting (seen 3 times): Repeating failure. Investigate the root cause rather than the symptom.
- [idea, S] Offer a monthly 'site + care' plan with a low setup fee
  Why: A Mumbai freelancer sells local businesses four subscription tiers. They run from Rs 2,499 to Rs 12,999 a month, with one-time setup fees of Rs 3,999 to Rs 14,999. Hosting and maintenance are included, there is no lock-in, and upgrading costs only the setup difference. The Starter tier is a 3-page site with a WhatsApp button and Search Console setup. Business adds Google Business Profile setup and a monthly report. This is one competitor's published pricing, not proof of demand. Tiga currently has no recurring revenue: the money numbers show 0 open deals and 0 paid this month.
  Benefit: A small first payment makes it easier for a shop owner to say yes. Monthly income also smooths out the gaps between projects. It builds on the approved GBP tune-up and review-QR offers.
  First step: Write a 3-tier Tiga plan on the rate card. Starter would be site, WhatsApp button and hosting. Business would add the GBP tune-up and a monthly photo refresh. Growth would add review requests and a monthly report. Add it to the proposal template, and set the setup fee below the competitor's to suit Bengaluru shops.
  Sources: https://asadfaizee.is-a.dev/services
- [improvement, M] Add an 'AI-search and service-page readiness' check to the Analyst and audit sheet
  Why: Whitespark's 2026 local ranking survey added an AI search visibility score. Its top factors are presence on expert 'best of' lists, a dedicated page for each service, and citations on industry sites. The same survey ranks GBP predefined services higher than before, at #22. The board already has a GBP category check and an on-page SEO check. Neither looks at service pages or predefined services, and the survey says a business needs both.
  Benefit: Each audit sheet gains a concrete, visible gap to name in the cold email, such as 'no page for your haircut or facial services'. It also gives a natural upsell: one service page per service.
  First step: In the Analyst's site check, list the site's pages and match their titles against the prospect's category keywords. Flag 'no service pages' and 'no predefined services on the GBP', and print both on the audit sheet next to the Google listing checklist.
  Sources: https://whitespark.ca/whats-working-in-local-seo
- [improvement, S] Make photo editing for shop listings real-photo only, and say so in the offer
  Why: The Whitespark survey ranks clear, non-stock photo and video quality at #45 for the local pack. It lists AI-generated photos on a profile as a negative factor. It also says a steady flow of reviews that include photos matters (#43). The 'photo refresh' offer already on the board depends on the photo-editing skill. If that skill generated or heavily altered images, it could hurt the shops it is meant to help.
  Benefit: Protects clients' Google listings and gives Tiga a trust-building line: 'real photos of your shop, only cleaned up'. It also lets the review-QR card ask for photos in reviews.
  First step: Add a rule to the photo-editing skill: crop, light, colour and background cleanup only, with no generated or stock imagery. Put the same sentence on the photo-refresh rate card, and add 'add a photo' to the review-request WhatsApp text.
  Sources: https://whitespark.ca/whats-working-in-local-seo
- [idea, S] Show shops a 'steady reviews and open-hours' scorecard in the free listing check
  Why: The Whitespark survey ranks 'business is open at time of search' as a new top-5 factor. A steady influx of reviews over time (#14) matters more than bursts, and review recency is #11. It warns against listing hours the business doesn't keep. Many small Bengaluru shops are unlikely to have hours that match how they actually trade, so this is easy to check by hand on a walk-in.
  Benefit: Gives the owner two quick, checkable talking points on walk-ins, with no software needed. It leads naturally into the review-QR add-on and the monthly plan.
  First step: Add two lines to the printable audit sheet: 'hours match real opening times (check the shop's board)' and 'date of the latest Google review'. Fill them in during the next walk-in route.
  Sources: https://whitespark.ca/whats-working-in-local-seo
